issues.sourceTitle: Build the elicitation harness to milestone one — an interview that produces a validated artifact with per-value provenance
issues.oldOuter:
The [elicitation kernel spec](<https://github.com/hashintel/brunch-lite/blob/main/docs/planning/elicitation-kernel/spec.md>) is finished and reviewed, but nothing has been built — the repo holds planning documents and no code at all. Until that changes, the September demo has no library to consume: FE-1362 committed the demo to a purpose-built shell driving a new interviewing library, and this is that library.

Milestone one is the walking version of the whole architecture. A person is interviewed in ordinary conversation; the agent captures what they said as evidence-anchored structured meaning; a plugin turns those captures into a real artifact — a Gherkin feature file for the first target — in which every value traces back to a verbatim quote, corrections never erase history, and anything that could not be represented is reported rather than dropped. The sub-issues below are vertical slices of that path, each one demoable or verifiable on its own.

One capability is deliberately absent. The spec requires a second, harder target to stress the plugin contract before that contract is declared stable, and which target that should be depends on decisions still being resolved on FE-1357 — so the plugin interface stays explicitly unfrozen through this batch, and the last four tickets are a working plan rather than a settled one.

issues.sourceTitle: Generative test corpus over the replay driver
issues.proposedTitle: Generate replay tests for the harness rules
issues.proposedOuter:
Earlier work has accumulated hand-written replay tests, while the ten harness rules are stated as properties. This task will derive generated conversations and values from plugin declarations, run the rules against those sequences without a model or runtime dependency, and retain reduced failures as regression cases.

The amount of generation needed for milestone one, the role of offline model-generated fixtures, and the fixture refresh process still need decisions.
issues.innerRecord:
## What to build

Turn the hand-written tests accumulated by the earlier slices into seeds for a generated corpus. The ten harness invariants are literally properties; the generators come from a plugin's declarations rather than its implementation; and conversations themselves become generated command sequences, so pathological interview shapes get found rather than imagined.

Spec: §14.4 (testing strategy), §14.1 (the ten invariants), §12.4 (SDK testing surface).

## Not yet ready for an agent

Approved in shape, foggy in detail. Worth settling first: how much generative machinery earns its keep at milestone one versus after a second plugin exists; whether the model-as-offline-generator step is in scope now or is a later luxury; and what the regenerate-on-declaration-change workflow actually looks like in practice.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The ten harness invariants run as executable properties, not as prose
- [ ] Arbitraries derive from Valibot declarations rather than implementations, so a plugin cannot accidentally test itself against its own bugs
- [ ] Negative-space properties hold for plugin code: validators total, and projection never emitting an undeclared loss category
- [ ] Command-sequence testing runs over the envelope-derived alphabet — utter, settle-range, sweep, correct, contradict, reply-with-absence, redirect
- [ ] Mutation operators generalise the minimal-pairs idea: epistemic-status flips, absence injections, supersession injections
- [ ] A model plays respondent as an offline generator whose outputs freeze as replayable fixtures — never as a CI oracle; everything in CI runs with no model and no substrate
- [ ] Fixtures regenerate when declarations change, and the staleness is detectable rather than silent
- [ ] Shrunk counterexamples are pinned as regressions and read as type-design feedback

issues.sourceTitle: Dev app — target gallery and diagnostic probe surface
issues.proposedTitle: Expand the dev app into a target gallery and diagnostic view
issues.proposedOuter:
The dev app currently serves as a test UI. This task will make it support local development, side-by-side target demonstrations, and a diagnostic view of session state, tool traffic, suspensions, and injected signals.

The required diagnostic depth, the timing of a gallery before a second target exists, and the actions a colleague must perform without help remain unsettled.
issues.innerRecord:
## What to build

Promote the dev app from a test surface into the chartered three-role vehicle the spec describes: the local development loop, a colleague-facing gallery where several targets can be demoed side by side, and a diagnostic view that shows the machinery rather than only the chat.

The diagnostic role is the one worth protecting. It exists because reacting to a system's internals is a different activity from reacting to its conversation, and the fog note that surfaced it asked for parallel state readout with labelled moving parts — pending slot, high-water mark, tool traffic, suspension boundaries, injected signals.

Spec: §12.5 (dev app roles, deferred ui package), §7.6 (renderer seam), §12.1 (host-authored agent module).

## Not yet ready for an agent

Approved in shape, foggy in detail. Worth settling first: how much of the exploded-view instrumentation belongs here versus later; whether the gallery is genuinely needed before a second target exists to gallery; and what a colleague is meant to be able to do unaided.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The local dev loop runs against the available plugins with one agent per target and static per-agent tool sets
- [ ] Parallel tabbed sessions work across targets without cross-contamination
- [ ] The diagnostic surface shows per-session state and tool traffic alongside the conversation, with the moving parts labelled
- [ ] Affordance renderers live in the dev app, with the ui affordance package deliberately deferred
- [ ] Remote-parity constraints are visibly respected: one agent serving many conversations, pinned agent name, storage port owned outside the plugin, no dynamic agent creation

issues.sourceTitle: Verify compaction leaves the durable entry projection intact
issues.proposedTitle: Test durable history across transcript compaction
issues.proposedOuter:
The specification says transcript compaction may reduce model context without removing entries that evidence references resolve, but no test has crossed a real compaction boundary. This investigation will determine whether old evidence pointers and session state survive, then record either confirmation or the exact archive work the binding must perform.

The test design depends in part on whether Flue provides a compaction definition.
issues.innerRecord:
## What to build

An answer to the one durability claim in the spec that nothing has tested. Pi-family substrates compact long transcripts, and the spec asserts that compaction may shrink what the model re-reads but never what the store can resolve. No prototype has ever driven a session across a compaction boundary, so the assertion is currently unverified.

The outcome is knowledge, not a feature: either the durable entry projection survives compaction unmodified, or we learn exactly what the binding has to preserve itself and the archive mechanism absorbs it.

Spec: §9.7 (context compaction versus the durable log), §14.5 (open verification items).

## Not yet ready for an agent

Approved in shape, foggy in detail — and partly dependent on whether Flue ships a compaction definition at all, which is worth establishing before designing the test.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A session is genuinely driven across a compaction boundary, not simulated
- [ ] Evidence pointers created before compaction still resolve afterwards
- [ ] Either the durable projection is confirmed compaction-independent, or the entries compaction prunes are enumerated and the archive's absorption of them is verified
- [ ] Per-session harness state is confirmed to live outside the transcript and survive
- [ ] If a compaction definition is supplied, injected signals and affordance tool parts are confirmed to need no protected status
- [ ] The finding is written up and the spec section updated from unverified to settled either way

issues.sourceTitle: Author the second pack and freeze the plugin contract
issues.proposedTitle: Choose a second target and stabilize the plugin interface
issues.proposedOuter:
Gherkin alone cannot establish a stable plugin interface because it does not exercise evidence grading, graph-shaped payloads, or derived domain labels. This task will build a harder second target through the same harness, record the interface changes it requires, and then judge the interface against the specified proof obligations.

FE-1364 must first choose between the specified assurance-argument target and the demo's process-model target; that choice also determines whether this work is demo-critical.
issues.innerRecord:
## What to build

The ticket that makes the plugin contract real. A second, harder target gets authored against the SDK, stressing the parts a Gherkin file never touches — evidence grading, a payload graph rather than a flat list, derived domain labels — and only once it has done so is the export surface declared stable.

**Which second target is not yet decided, and is not this ticket's to decide.** The spec names an assurance-argument plugin and specifies it in buildable detail. But FE-1362 committed the September demo to a process-model plugin, which would make that the natural second target and leave assurance as specified-but-unbuilt. The answer depends on FE-1364, and it changes this ticket's urgency as well as its content: if the second target is the process-model plugin, this stops being milestone-one cleanup and becomes demo-critical path.

Spec: §13 (portfolio and hybrid order), §13.2–13.3 (the assurance argument, if that is the target), §14.2–14.3 (proof obligations, gating tests), §11.5 (generic strategy quiver).

## Not yet ready for an agent

Blocked on FE-1364 for the target decision. A working plan, not a settled one.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The second target is chosen, with the reasoning recorded
- [ ] Its packs are authored and it runs end to end through the same harness, sharing no code with the gherkin plugin beyond the SDK
- [ ] The reprojection gating test passes: capture once, project into materially different targets, verify agreement
- [ ] The black-box authoring test runs — public SDK and docs handed to someone who has not read core, counting concepts, boilerplate, and escape hatches
- [ ] Every contract change the second target forced is recorded, since each one is evidence about what gherkin alone failed to stress
- [ ] Any interviewing technique that turned out to operate on envelope vocabulary rather than domain vocabulary is identified as candidate strategy-quiver content rather than buried in a plugin pack
- [ ] The five proof obligations are judged against the hourglass, and the SDK export surface is declared stable

issues.sourceTitle: Scaffold the Bun workspace and prove the CI smoke
issues.proposedTitle: Create the Bun workspace and enforce dependency boundaries
issues.proposedOuter: The repository needs a Bun workspace that builds and tests from a clean checkout before feature work begins. This task will create the specified core, Flue binding, Gherkin plugin, and dev-app boundaries, then enforce their dependency direction in CI without model credentials or network access.
issues.innerRecord:
## What to build

A Bun-workspace monorepo that builds and tests green from empty, with the architectural boundaries in place from the first commit rather than retrofitted later. Nothing user-visible happens yet; what this delivers is that every later slice lands into a structure that already refuses the wrong dependency direction.

Spec: §12.2 (package topology), §12.3 (naming), §12.4 (schemas), §12.5 (CI smoke), §10 (recorded Flue facts the implementation must respect).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `bun test` and `vite build` both pass from a clean checkout, with no model key and no network access
- [ ] Packages exist per the spec's topology with its role prefixes: `core` (plugin SDK as its export surface) with a `core/testing` subpath, `binding-flue`, `plugin-gherkin`, and a dev app owning the agent module, mount, and conversation store
- [ ] The dependency invariants hold and are mechanically checkable, not just documented: plugins resolve `core` only — never the binding, never Flue; `core` imports no substrate; the binding imports both
- [ ] Valibot is the schema library at every boundary; no Standard-Schema conversion seam
- [ ] The recorded Flue constraints are respected by construction: vite pinned to ^8, `'use agent'` as the agent module's first statement, `agentName` a pinned string literal
- [ ] Tool-name prefix derives from the product name and bakes in neither "elicit" nor "brunch"

issues.sourceTitle: Walking skeleton — the harness asks a free-text question and binds the reply
issues.proposedTitle: Implement the first suspended free-text question
issues.proposedOuter: The harness needs to ask a free-text question, suspend the turn, receive a typed answer, and continue a real dev-app conversation. This task will move the proven prototype mechanism into the main workspace while keeping the question out of instructions and binding replies mechanically to the single pending affordance.
issues.innerRecord:
## What to build

The first thing a person can actually use: open the dev app, and the agent asks a free-text question, waits, receives the typed answer, and carries on the conversation with the answer in hand. This is the turn-suspension protocol the harness has to own because Flue has no ask-the-user primitive, proven in the real tree rather than on a prototype branch.

The prototype on `prototype/10-flue-roundtrip` already established the mechanism; this ports it in and hardens the two rulings that came after it — no instruction interpolation, and mechanical reply binding.

Spec: §7.1–7.4, §7.7, §9.2 (pending-affordance slot), §10 capabilities 1–5, §12.1.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A person can hold a multi-turn conversation in the dev app in which the agent asks free-text questions and receives answers
- [ ] Turn suspension works through a terminating ask tool plus the pending affordance in per-session state, with the answer arriving as a fresh dispatch
- [ ] The pending question is never interpolated into instructions — it rides the ask tool's result — and no "instructions updated" advisory wake occurs per ask (spec §14.5 wake-wart residue: confirm no other instruction-state write path re-triggers it)
- [ ] Reply binding is harness-mechanical off the single-pending invariant: no echo token, no reliance on the model remembering an id
- [ ] Durable affordance identity and payload ride the ask tool's output part, not the data channel
- [ ] A second interactive affordance in the same batch is rejected as mechanism, not as instruction
- [ ] Every question renders through the markdown floor, so a ui that knows only the envelope shows something usable

issues.sourceTitle: Capture envelope, storage port, and the local capture store
issues.proposedTitle: Implement capture history and local persistence
issues.proposedOuter: The harness needs a local store for captures, corrections, contradictions, retractions, and resolution records that never overwrites history. This task will define the capture envelope and persistence port, derive status when reading, reject invalid lifecycle changes, and apply each sweep atomically without requiring a model or runtime.
issues.innerRecord:
## What to build

The capture store and the envelope that sits in it — drivable end to end from tests with no model and no substrate, which is the whole point of the design. You can write a capture, correct it, contradict it, retract it, and read back a coherent history in which nothing was silently overwritten and every status was computed rather than stored.

Spec: §5 (capture envelope), §5.1 (absence states), §6.2 (envelope-level validation), §8.3–8.5 (idempotence, supersession, resolution records), §9.6 (the storage port), §10 capability 10.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The storage port is harness-defined and binding-implemented; nothing in the plugin surface can reach persistence
- [ ] The envelope carries a harness-minted id alongside a content-derived dedup key that excludes epistemic status, so re-reading the same evidence differently requires explicit supersession
- [ ] Value-XOR-absence is enforced as a refusal, and the six absence states are distinct capture values that never collapse into null or negation
- [ ] Supersession is single-hop over active heads only; superseding an already-superseded capture is refused, and that refusal carries the world-moved facts
- [ ] Superseded captures stay inspectable forever and never read as active
- [ ] A `conflicting` issue closes only through a resolution record citing the true user's utterance; a bare close is refused, and so is a record citing the agent's words
- [ ] Retraction is an explicit stored event citing the user, naming no successor, and is the only path to retracted status
- [ ] No status field is stored anywhere — envelope status derives at read time from links, records, and events
- [ ] Writes are serialized and application is whole-sweep-atomic: a sweep applies entirely or refuses entirely
- [ ] Harness invariants 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, and 10 hold as executable tests

This task will define the capture envelope and persistence port, derive status when reading, reject invalid lifecycle changes, and apply each sweep atomically without requiring a model or runtime.

issues.sourceTitle: Durable entry projection, harness-resolved anchoring, and the session-log archive
issues.proposedTitle: Resolve evidence quotes to durable conversation entries
issues.proposedOuter: Captures must cite durable user entries, but the model is reliable with verbatim quotes rather than entry numbers. This task will resolve each quote against true user entries, reject missing or invalid evidence, retain every read entry in the archive, and keep cited entries retrievable independently of runtime history retention.
issues.innerRecord:
## What to build

The bridge between a live conversation and the store: given a session someone has actually talked into, the harness can take a verbatim quote and work out which entry it came from — and can keep those entries retrievable forever, independently of whatever the substrate decides to retain.

This exists because the model cannot be trusted with entry numbers and can be trusted with quotes. Ticket 13's HITL rounds on the prior map found the model's quotes flawless and its sequence guesses never once convergent, so anchoring is harness-resolved and entry identity never appears in the model-facing contract.

Spec: §5 (evidence spans), §8.2 (harness-resolved anchoring), §9.4 (provenance), §9.6 (session-log archive), §10 capability 8.

- [ ] The binding can read the session's durable entry projection with provenance-discriminating entry kinds, absorbing the absence of an in-process API

issues.sourceTitle: Settlement trigger and sweep — the first captured statement
issues.proposedOuter: The harness can ask questions but cannot yet turn a completed topic into stored meaning. This task will detect an unswept conversation range, let the agent judge whether it has settled, and store quote-anchored captures through an atomic operation that is safe to repeat. It will also preserve the high-water mark and report unanswered asks without blocking capture.
issues.innerRecord:
## What to build

The slice the whole architecture is for. You say something in conversation; the agent judges that the topic has closed; it sweeps what you said into the store as captures anchored to your actual words; and the sweep is safe to run twice. After this ticket the system genuinely elicits — it just has nothing domain-shaped to do with the result yet.

Spec: §8.1 (settlement trigger and judgment), §8.3 (sweep idempotence), §8.6 (unaccounted-ask advisory), §6.4 (cadence as policy), §10 capabilities 7 and 9.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A conversation about something substantive produces captures in the store, each anchored to a verbatim quote from the person's own turns
- [ ] Settlement decomposes into trigger and judgment: the harness computes the unswept tail and steers a settlement-check signal into a same-response continuation turn; the agent decides whether the range has settled, and declining is legal
- [ ] The trigger's two guards hold — it fires on suspensions too, so a pending affordance suppresses the nudge; and it never re-nudges the same latest user entry
- [ ] Re-sweeping a range creates no duplicate captures and does repair omissions, because identity is content-keyed rather than range-keyed — load-bearing under at-least-once tool re-execution

issues.sourceTitle: Plugin SDK and the gherkin plugin — the first projected artifact
issues.proposedTitle: Produce the first Gherkin artifact through the plugin SDK
issues.proposedOuter:
The first complete artifact should turn an interview about a feature into a valid Gherkin file and a typed report of information Gherkin cannot represent. This task will implement the pure plugin operations, injected harness context, authoring packs, validation, and failure atomicity needed for that path.

The SDK remains unstable until a harder second target tests the interface.
issues.innerRecord:
## What to build

The first end-to-end artifact. Someone is interviewed about a feature and gets back a valid Gherkin feature file, together with an honest report of everything they said that the file could not represent. This is where the plugin contract stops being a design and starts being something a plugin author actually programs against.

**Explicit non-goal: this ticket does not freeze the plugin contract.** Gherkin is the trivial target, and the spec's two-targets rule forbids letting it fix the interface before a hard target has stressed it. Build the SDK surface, exercise it, and leave it declared unstable.

Spec: §6.1 (operations and calling convention), §4 (inversion of control, PluginContext), §11.1–11.3 (what a plugin owns, pack form, smallest honest plugin), §13.1 (gherkin).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An interview about a feature yields a parse-valid `.feature` file plus a typed loss report using the declared vocabulary
- [ ] The four operations are pure and snapshot-in/deltas-out: they receive an immutable snapshot and return observations, issues, and deltas; the harness validates and applies; no operation addresses storage, the user, or the model
- [ ] Harness capabilities reach the plugin only through a narrow injected PluginContext, and milestone one defines no storage-addressable methods on it at all
- [ ] The plugin ships an ElicitationPack — kernel cards, completion contract, clarification hints — and a ProjectionPack with required project and validate, authored to the `writing-for-agents` standard and Principle v2
- [ ] Validation is parse validity plus an optional pack-declared step-lexicon check, needing no external project
- [ ] Validators are total: they never throw, and always return typed issues
- [ ] Issues are namespaced to their producer, so a target-originated requirement never silently reads as a harness-level one
- [ ] A failed operation leaves no partially applied deltas
- [ ] The smallest-honest-plugin bar is checked, not assumed: a flat record list plus one validator must suffice, and every contract addition made here is justified against the bar it raises
- [ ] The SDK export surface is documented as unstable pending a second target

issues.sourceTitle: Conflict, supersession, and the interpretation render
issues.proposedTitle: Preserve conflicts until the user resolves them
issues.proposedOuter: When a person contradicts an earlier statement, both interpretations must remain visible until the person resolves the conflict. This task will store the alternatives and resolution evidence, distinguish correction paths, and render the harness's interpretation with uncertainty intact. It will also keep interactive questions separate from informational renders and distinguish answered, redirected, and unanswered outcomes.
issues.innerRecord:
## What to build

What happens when someone changes their mind or contradicts themselves. Say something, say something incompatible later, and both readings stay live and visible until you explicitly settle which one holds — the system never quietly picks. Alongside it, the one affordance the harness must own itself: the render that shows you what it thinks you said, with the uncertainty intact.

Spec: §6.3 (issues versus advisories), §7.5 (transport outcomes), §7.6 (interpretation render), §8.4–8.5 (supersession channels, resolution records).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Contradicting yourself surfaces a `conflicting` issue with both interpretations live as alternatives, and neither is silently dropped
- [ ] Resolving it produces a resolution record citing your own words; the winning capture keeps its original epistemic status and authority lives in the record
- [ ] The two supersession channels are distinguishable in the store: a creation-time link for sweep-time correction, a resolution record for issue-time adjudication between existing alternatives
- [ ] The interpretation render is harness-owned and shows envelope vocabulary — epistemic status, absence states, live alternatives, derived status — with a plain JSON default and a plugin-optional typed renderer seam that is actually exercised by the gherkin plugin
- [ ] Non-interactive renders ride their own tool output parts and never contend for the affordance slot, so an ask and a render in one batch cannot clobber each other
- [ ] Transport outcomes record as answered, redirected, or unanswered, distinct from epistemic absence; a topic change mid-question reads as redirected
- [ ] Advisories are computed and ephemeral — never stored, never blocking — and issues are stored and close only explicitly
- [ ] Harness invariants 1, 2, and 6 hold as executable tests

issues.sourceTitle: The full affordance set — choices, questionnaire chaining, and the absence strip
issues.proposedTitle: Add choices, questionnaires, and explicit absence replies
issues.proposedOuter:
The harness currently has only free-text questions. This task will add single-choice, multi-choice, and locally chained questionnaires, plus explicit replies for unknown, inapplicable, and deferred answers.

Because inbound replies are strings, the transport must distinguish a UI action from identical typed prose; clients that only render markdown will continue to produce honestly inferred absences.
issues.innerRecord:
## What to build

The rest of the ways the harness can ask something. Beyond free text: pick one, pick several, and a questionnaire that walks several questions locally without a model turn between them. Plus the absence strip — the one-tap way to say "I don't know", "doesn't apply", or "decide later" — and the transport mechanism that makes a tap genuinely distinguishable from typed prose.

That last part is load-bearing and easy to get wrong. Inbound replies are string-only, so a bare string cannot tell a one-tap "not applicable" from someone typing the words. Tap-ness has to be a transport fact or the system will claim certainty it hasn't earned.

Spec: §7.2 (baseline forms, questionnaire chaining, markdown floor), §5.1 (absence states, reserved reply encoding), §7.7 (recorded transport facts).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Single-choice and multi-choice questions work end to end, rendering and returning through the same evidence path as free text
- [ ] A questionnaire is one affordance with N steps: the payload carries all the questions, the ui walks them locally, answers return individually or batched, and no intermediate model turns occur
- [ ] The absence strip's three labels map onto their absence states, and absences land as first-class capture values
- [ ] A reply parsing as the reserved encoding, arriving while its affordance is pending, is transport-explicit; every other reply is conversational and yields absences marked inferred
- [ ] Structured taps are optional for a ui, not required: a ui affording only the markdown floor produces no encoding and honestly yields inferred-only absences
- [ ] Plugin custom forms register as progressive enhancement keyed on form tag, with payloads opaque at the tool boundary and validated harness-side against plugin declarations on read-back
- [ ] Every form carries a markdown floor
- [ ] Deferred and declined behave differently downstream: completion evaluation chases a deferral and treats a decline as a boundary that only an explicit act can close

issues.sourceTitle: Re-entry briefing, resume reconciliation, and restart durability
issues.proposedTitle: Restore interview context after resume and restart
issues.proposedOuter: A returning interview must reflect captures, conflicts, unswept conversation, and a pending question that changed while the agent was away. This task will compute and inject that briefing, preserve all session state through restart, and prevent injected system facts from being cited as user evidence. Completion remains derived when reading, so a later correction follows the normal path.
issues.innerRecord:
## What to build

Coming back. Quit an interview halfway, restart the process, return later, and the agent picks up knowing what changed while it was away — what was captured or superseded, which issues opened or closed, what was left unswept, and which question is still hanging. It says so in the conversation rather than pretending continuity.

The subtle requirement is that the briefing must be in the log honestly without ever becoming evidence. It is injected on the user's behalf, so it looks like the user's side of the conversation — and a capture citing it would launder the system's own words into the person's mouth.

Spec: §9.1–9.3 (durable document, per-session state, re-entry briefing), §9.4 (provenance), §9.5 (completion derived), §8.7 (resume-time sweep reconciliation), §14.5 (restart durability).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Resuming a session after the world moved injects a state message whose content is computed facts only: unswept tail, captures created or superseded and issues opened or closed since this session last swept, open issues, pending unanswered affordance
- [ ] The briefing is advisory — it forces nothing, and the agent weighs it
- [ ] A minimal user-visible insertion notice accompanies every injected state message
- [ ] Injected entries project as structurally non-user, so citing one as evidence is mechanically refused rather than merely discouraged
- [ ] An unswept tail left by a session that ended between judgment and sweep surfaces on resume, and the agent judges whether to sweep before proceeding
- [ ] The briefing works in all three shapes: fresh session, resumed session, and post-restart
- [ ] Full-stack durability holds with a real conversation store: captures, session logs, high-water mark, and pending slot all survive a process restart
- [ ] A new session binds to its target-document through immutable creation data; dispatching an existing conversation id resumes against the document's current state
- [ ] Completion is a read-time derived status with no lock and no terminal state — someone returning with a correction after "done" is handled normally

issues.sourceTitle: Make the CI gates and dev app fail loudly where review found they fail silently
issues.oldOuter: The FE-1361 code review swept the whole repo and verified five findings that fall outside that ticket's scope. Three sit in the merge gates themselves: the checks that are supposed to keep workspace boundaries honest can currently go red on an innocent comment-only edit, silently skip any newly added workspace group, and let a misspelled tool operation name compile — so the gates either cry wolf or pass vacuously, which matters most in a repo whose gates are its main safety net. The other two are silent-failure seams in the dev app: a route path duplicates the one identifier the codebase pins as never-drifting, and the production asset route serves a narrower set of files than the client build can emit, so the first added font or image would break production only. All five have verified failure scenarios; each fix is small and none blocks current work.
issues.proposedTitle: Fix verified silent failures in CI and the dev app
issues.proposedOuter:
The FE-1361 review confirmed five small failures outside that issue's scope. Three CI checks can reject harmless text, omit new workspace groups, or accept misspelled tool operations; two dev-app routes duplicate a pinned identifier or fail on asset types the client build may emit.

This task will make those checks and routes report the verified failures without changing unrelated behavior; none currently blocks other work.
issues.innerRecord:
## Findings (verified by the FE-1361 review, 2026-08-13)

1. `test/boundaries.test.ts:218` — agent-module detection is a bare substring match for `'use agent'` over raw file text, so a comment mentioning the directive turns any dev source file into an "agent module" and fails two assertions (CI red on a comment-only change; `test/build-artifact.test.ts:44` shares the filter). Fix: anchor detection to the first statement — the comment-stripping logic at lines 231–233 already exists.
2. `test/workspace.ts:49` — `workspacePackages()` hardcodes `[packages, apps]` instead of deriving from (or asserting agreement with) root `package.json`'s `workspaces` globs, so a new workspace group escapes every boundary invariant as a vacuous pass; `directoriesIn()` also returns `[]` for a missing parent, so a renamed group degrades silently. Fix: assert the hardcoded group set equals the workspaces globs.
3. `packages/core/src/naming.ts:60` — `toolName(operation)` takes plain `string` instead of the `Operation` union exported two lines above (the union has zero consumers), so `toolName('aks')` compiles and ships a misnamed model-facing tool. Fix: narrow the parameter type.
4. `apps/dev/src/app.ts:19` — the mount path hardcodes `'brunch-gherkin-elicitor'` although `GherkinElicitor.agentName` is imported in the same file; a copy-pasted second agent would shadow the mount while tests stay green. Fix: `` app.route(`/agents/${GherkinElicitor.agentName}`, …) ``.
5. `apps/dev/src/app.ts:36` — the production `/assets/:file` route allowlists only `.js|.css|.map` and reads hits as UTF-8, so any other emitted asset 404s in production (works in vite dev), and extending the allowlist without switching to a Buffer read would corrupt binary bytes.

issues.sourceTitle: Close the seams where the capture store and verification gates claim more than they enforce
issues.oldOuter:
An inductive review of the open PR comments (2026-08-14) found two seams that still claim more than their implementations support. The capture store applies different rule sets at command time, persisted-parse time, and lifecycle-transition time — so a command can return success for a snapshot the next read rejects, and an open conflict can end up with no legal way to close. The plan is a nine-commit queue that gives each contract one owner and makes negative results precise; it is authored and ready to execute.

issues.sourceTitle: The affordance protocol survives retries, unknown forms, and abandoned asks
issues.oldOuter:
The FE-1389 deep-read (notes/deep-read-fe-1389.md, from the FE-1401 remediation sweep) found three places where the new ask/affordance protocol fails unsafely rather than safely. Flue re-executes tools at-least-once, and a re-executed ask mints the identical affordance — but the pending-slot guard checks only that the slot is occupied, so a benign retry is refused as if the model had asked a second question. The dev UI validates the whole concrete free-text form and renders nothing on a parse failure, so the first affordance of any other form will blank instead of falling back to the markdown floor the spec requires (§7.2/§7.7 — the envelope needs its own schema with the payload opaque). And an ask whose reply never arrives occupies the slot forever: nothing records an `unanswered` outcome (§7.5) and no advisory reports the stuck state (§8.6), so every later ask is refused silently.

None of these blocks the walking skeleton — they are the hardening it deliberately deferred — but the retry refusal will start firing as soon as anything (like the settlement trigger) makes re-execution common, and the markdown floor breaks the moment a second affordance form lands.
issues.proposedTitle: Make affordance handling safe under retries and abandonment
issues.proposedOuter:
The FE-1389 review found three unsafe cases in the ask protocol. A retry of the same ask is rejected as a second question, an unknown form can blank the UI instead of showing markdown, and an abandoned ask can occupy the pending position forever.

These defects do not block the first free-text flow, but retries will become common with settlement and new forms will require the fallback. This task will make identical retries idempotent, parse the envelope separately from its opaque payload, and record unanswered outcomes so later asks can proceed.

1. **Retry misreported as duplicate ask** — `packages/binding-flue/src/index.ts` pending-slot updater tests `current !== null`; should tolerate `current.id === affordance.id` (id is deterministic in `toolCallId`, so re-execution is detectable). One-line fix + a test that replays the same tool call.
2. **Markdown floor absent in the UI** — `apps/dev/src/ui/chat.tsx` `safeParse(FreeTextAffordance, part.data)` returns null on failure. Needs an envelope-only schema (id / form / markdown, payload opaque) rendered as the fallback; ticket 10 §5 proved the intended behavior.
3. **No escape from an occupied slot** — slot clears only on `kind: 'user'` delivery; spec §7.5's `unanswered` outcome and §8.6's unaccounted-ask advisory are the intended relief valves, neither exists.

The walking skeleton placed reusable ask behavior inside the Flue binding, including identity, the one-live rule, reply signals, and instruction text. A second runtime binding would have to reproduce that behavior, and settlement work would deepen the duplication.

This task will extract pure ask decisions and builders into core while leaving only Flue hook translation in the binding. It is scheduled before FE-1392 so new settlement behavior begins in the portable module.
issues.innerRecord:

* Acceptance: binding-flue/src/index.ts contains no protocol decisions, only hook translation; the walking-skeleton integration test (do-not-weaken) stays green unmodified — it pins behavior, not placement.
* Blocks FE-1392 by design (sequencing: docs/planning/_shared/CONVERGENCE.md, second evaluation).
